items.h3: First Disposal in an Older Kitchen
items.body: Some kitchens in Elgin's older homes never had one. We check the drain size, the dishwasher connection and the power under the sink before quoting.
A west side home from the 1990s or 2000s may be on its first or second disposal. Most last about 8 to 15 years.
A disposal that drains slowly often means the line behind it is coated with grease. We check it while we're there.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: How do I unjam my garbage disposal?
items.preview: Turn off the power, then use the hex key on the bottom.
items.answer: Turn off the switch and unplug it or shut off the breaker. Many units have a hex socket on the bottom: turn it back and forth with the wrench that came with it. Press the reset button and try again. If it's still stuck, call us.

items.preview: Jams and loose connections are repairs. A leaking housing or dead motor means replace.
items.answer: A jam, a tripped reset or a loose connection can be fixed. A disposal leaking from its housing or with a burned-out motor needs replacing.

items.q: What shouldn't go down the disposal?
items.preview: Grease, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
items.answer: Grease and oil, bones, fibrous scraps like celery and corn husks, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.

items.q: Can you add a disposal to a sink that never had one?
items.preview: Usually. We check the drain, dishwasher hookup and power first.
items.answer: Usually. We check the drain size, the dishwasher connection and whether there's a switched outlet under the sink. If power is needed, we'll tell you before the install.

items.answer: It depends on the unit and whether plumbing or electrical changes are needed. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
